note: Restriction archetypes. The client-specific part of a guideline is the parameter, not the logic. New mandates are coded as parameterized instances of these patterns rather than authored from scratch. In a production build this catalog would be derived empirically by mining rules already coded in the compliance engine, not hand-written.

archetypes.label: Issuer concentration limit
archetypes.notes: Watch for look-through language on funds and for aggregation across affiliated issuers.

archetypes.label: Sector exposure limit
archetypes.notes: Frequently expressed relative to benchmark weight rather than absolute.

archetypes.label: Country or region exposure limit
archetypes.notes: Confirm whether classification follows domicile, risk country, or index provider.

archetypes.label: Minimum credit quality
archetypes.notes: Test point matters enormously. At purchase and ongoing are different rules with different breach profiles.

archetypes.label: Portfolio duration band
archetypes.notes: Often stated as benchmark plus or minus a band rather than absolute.

archetypes.label: Prohibited instrument or asset class
archetypes.notes: Prohibitions carved back by permitted purpose are a frequent source of ambiguity.

archetypes.label: Client restricted list screen
archetypes.notes: Almost always references an external appendix. The rule is codeable; the list is an ongoing data feed and a separate operational dependency.

archetypes.label: Revenue-threshold exclusionary screen
archetypes.notes: Unusable without a named data vendor. If the clause omits one, escalate rather than guess.

archetypes.label: Tracking error limit
archetypes.notes: Ex ante and ex post are not interchangeable. If unstated, escalate.
